Built the new oracle at /home/patrickd/aegis/.claude/worktrees/wf_5648cdb4-a5f-4/oracles/syscall-negative. The README documents the probe protocol. The oracle appends `--path forkwasm|cordon [--stage zygote] --probe <name> --allow-dir <dir> [--target|--fd|--port]` to the subject command. The subject runs its own sandbox install and prints an "armed" JSON line just before the syscall. The outcome is then one of: a result JSON line, the process wait status, or, on the forkwasm child stage, the zygote's child-exit line.

There are 26 probes, each run at 3 stages (cordon, forkwasm child, forkwasm zygote), giving 77 cells. Before judging, every probe runs once with no sandbox, using the oracle's own binary, and the host facts are recorded: the AppArmor userns sysctls, unprivileged_bpf_disabled, io_uring_disabled, perf_event_paranoid, unprivileged_userfaultfd, ptrace_scope and the Landlock ABI.

Pass rules: the kill class passes only on death by SIGSYS. clone3 passes only on ENOSYS, and only if the unsandboxed control was not already ENOSYS. The Landlock probes pass on EACCES or SIGSYS. EPERM never passes. TCP_ULP is probed on an established TCP fd the oracle opens and passes in. PR_GET_DUMPABLE is read back in the zygote, the child and the cordon. Two positive probes (getpid, and opening a file inside the allowed dir) must succeed, so a sandbox that kills everything fails.
